paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this psalm, friend. David looks around and it seems like the honest people are gone. Everybody's smooth-talking, and the loudest voices are bragging that nobody is their master. If you've ever felt like you're the last straight shooter in the room, David gets it (Psalm 12:1-4).

But the LORD doesn't leave David alone with that feeling. He speaks up Himself: "For the cause of the oppressed and for the groaning of the needy, I will now arise," and He promises, "I will bring safety to him who yearns" (Psalm 12:5). Then David says the words of the LORD "are flawless, like silver refined in a furnace, like gold purified sevenfold" (Psalm 12:6). Flattering words come cheap and they change with the crowd. The LORD's words are the ones you can put your whole weight on.

So when the world gets loud with lies, go back to what the LORD has said. David ends by telling Him, "You, O LORD, will keep us; You will forever guard us from this generation" (Psalm 12:7). He also admits that "The wicked wander freely, and vileness is exalted among men" (Psalm 12:8). Both things are true at once, and the LORD's keeping is the one that lasts. That's why I keep my ovens ready and my ears open to His Word, baker.
